_meta.active: CITRIC ACID; MAGNESIUM OXIDE; SODIUM PICOSULFATE
_meta.indication: Combination of sodium picosulfate, a stimulant laxative, and magnesium oxide and anhydrous citric acid which form magnesium citrate, an osmotic laxative, indicated for cleansing of the colon as a preparation for colonoscopy in adults

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, multicenter, assessor-blinded, parallel-group, active-controlled non-inferiority study of split-dose PicoPrep versus HalfLytely/Bisacodyl Tablets Bowel Prep Kit
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients requiring an elective complete colonoscopy in preparation for the procedure
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of responders with successful colon cleansing (rated excellent or good on the Aronchick scale) assessed by blinded colonoscopists
pivotal_trials.result: PicoPrep responder rate 84.2% vs HalfLytely 74.9%; 95% CI of the difference (2.9%, 15.7%) — PicoPrep split dose superior to HalfLytely

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, multicenter, assessor-blinded, parallel-group, active-controlled non-inferiority study of day-before PicoPrep versus HalfLytely/Bisacodyl Tablets Bowel Prep Kit
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients requiring an elective complete colonoscopy in preparation for the procedure
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of responders with successful colon cleansing (rated excellent or good on the Aronchick scale) assessed by blinded colonoscopists
pivotal_trials.result: PicoPrep responder rate 82.9% vs HalfLytely 79.7%; 95% CI of the difference (-3.0%, 10.0%) — PicoPrep single dose non-inferior to HalfLytely

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>1%) are nausea, headache and vomiting. In Study 1 (Split-Dose): nausea 2.6% (PREPOPIK) vs 3.7%, headache 1.6% vs 1.7%, vomiting 1.0% vs 3.4%. Warnings include serious fluid and electrolyte abnormalities (which can lead to cardiac arrhythmias or seizures and renal impairment) and rare ischemic colitis.
target_moa: Sodium picosulfate is a prodrug converted by colonic bacteria to its active metabolite BHPM, a stimulant (cathartic) laxative; magnesium oxide and citric acid react in water to form magnesium citrate, an osmotic laxative that draws water into the bowel lumen to stimulate peristalsis and evacuation
modality: small molecule (fixed combination of sodium picosulfate, magnesium oxide and anhydrous citric acid)

rems.type: There is no REMS for this application; a Medication Guide is provided

advisory_committee.vote: An advisory committee meeting was not convened regarding this application

description.text: Expanded colonoscopy bowel preparation indication to include pediatric patients 9 years of age and older

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for the use of PREPOIK for cleansing of the colon as a preparation for colonoscopy in adults and pediatric patients 9 years of age and older.

summary.text: PREPOPIK was submitted as a Standard-review 505(b)(2) NDA and approved full (traditional) approval on the basis of two Phase 3 active-controlled non-inferiority trials; no accelerated approval, breakthrough, fast track, orphan, or priority designation applied, and no advisory committee was convened.
